'''Nigel Geoffrey Stocks''' (born 6 September 1964) is an English [[engineer]] and [[physicist]], notable for discovering [[suprathreshold stochastic resonance|suprathreshold stochastic resonance (SSR)]] and its application to [[cochlear implant]] technology.<ref>Mark D. McDonnell, Nigel G. Stocks, Charles E. M. Pearce, and Derek Abbott, ''Stochastic Resonance'', Cambridge University Press, 2008.</ref>

==Education==
He attended [[Bingley Grammar School]] before received a BSc in Applied Physics and Electronics (1987) and a PhD in (1991), under [[Peter V. E. McClintock]], at [[Lancaster University]], [[UK]], with a dissertation entitled ''Experiments in Stochastic Nonlinear Dynamics.''<ref>{{Cite web |title=Nigel Stocks - The Mathematics Genealogy Project |url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=76492 |access-date=2023-04-02 |website=www.mathgenealogy.org}}</ref>

==Selected publication==
* [[Mark D. McDonnell]], Nigel G. Stocks, [[Charles E. M. Pearce]], and [[Derek Abbott]], ''[[Stochastic resonance (book)|Stochastic Resonance]]'', [[Cambridge University Press]], 2008, {{ISBN|978-0-521-88262-0}}.
